sections.sectionSummaryBrief: These days are recalled and fulfilled each year with an ascending level of holiness, requiring increased preparation for the Giving of the Torah, especially the preparation of "Naaseh v'Nishma."

translations.translation: d)
And these days are recalled and fulfilled,
that in each and every year those matters return and are drawn down as they were the first time,
and moreover,
that in each year they are on a more elevated level,
for we ascend in holiness.
And since all matters depend on our actions and service,
therefore,
in each year we must add and ascend in holiness also in the preparations for the Giving of the Torah,
an addition in the matter of "and he encamped" in the singular, as one person with one heart, which was on Rosh Chodesh Sivan,
and likewise in the preparations that were after Rosh Chodesh Sivan
(for immediately after Rosh Chodesh, Moshe began to occupy himself with them regarding the matter of receiving the Torah),
and all the more so in the preparation of the precedence of "Naaseh" to "Nishma,"

which is the primary preparation for the Giving of the Torah, as is also understood from the fact that this preparation of the precedence of "Naaseh" to "Nishma" is on the fifth of Sivan, which is the eve of the sixth of Sivan, on which the Torah was given.
And it is,
that during the day they will contemplate the matter of the precedence of "Naaseh" to "Nishma,"
a contemplation that is appropriate and that brings to action,
that in every matter of service of G-d,
one must first of all fulfill it in actual deed
("Naaseh"),
and after this understand the matter with his intellect, emotions, and understanding
("Nishma").
And even though this day
(the fifth of Sivan)
is the eve of the festival, when there are many preoccupations with preparations for the needs of the holiday,
nevertheless, the teaching of my revered father-in-law, the Rebbe, is known,
that on the festival of Shavuos and likewise on the eve
(and the like)
of the festival of Shavuos, there is no dominion
(so much)
of the opposing side,
and therefore it is a time fit to do everything for the benefit of Torah study and service, etc.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: In addition to the preparations for the days before Shavuos, there must be special effort regarding matters of the festival itself, including hearing the Ten Commandments and making resolutions to increase Torah study.

translations.translation: And it is simply understood,
that in addition to the aforementioned preparations that pertain to the days before the festival of Shavuos,
beginning from Rosh Chodesh Sivan,
there must be, all the more so, a special effort regarding the matters that pertain to the festival of Shavuos itself,
beginning with the effort that each and every Jew,
men, women, and children,
should be in the synagogue at the time of the reading of the Ten Commandments,
and as has been discussed several times,
that this—that each year on the festival of Shavuos the Torah is given anew, in a manner similar to how it was the first time—is revealed primarily in the reading of the Ten Commandments,
as the Sages said,
"The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: My children, read this portion every year, and I will consider it for you as if you are standing before Mount Sinai and receiving the Torah,"
therefore one must hear this portion with awe and fear, etc., as if standing before Mount Sinai,
and this is also one of the reasons for the great effort that all of Israel,
even the very young
(and)
should be in the synagogue at the time of the reading of the Ten Commandments,
as has been discussed at length several times
[And to add,
that the effort that the children should be in the synagogue at the time of the reading of the Ten Commandments also relates to the preparation of "our children are our guarantors,"
which can be said to include both the interpretation of "guarantors" as a mixture, that all of Israel are intermingled with one another,
and "guarantors" as sweetness and pleasantness, that all of Israel are guarantors and sweet to one another].
And likewise, good resolutions to increase in Torah study,
the revealed aspect of Torah and the inner aspect of Torah,
and until "your springs will spread forth outward,"
including also the effort to organize Torah gatherings on the day after the festival of Shavuos, the time of the giving of our Torah, or on the days close to it.
And as mentioned above,
that in each year we must add in all these matters with greater strength and vigor,
both regarding the preparations that pertain to the days before the time of the giving of our Torah,
and regarding good resolutions
(and the effort)
regarding the matters that pertain to the time of the giving of our Torah and the days after it.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Each year the preparations for the Giving of the Torah, especially "Naaseh v'Nishma," must be increased, leading to an incomparably higher level of the Giving of the Torah itself, particularly in this year before a year of miracles.

translations.translation: And as mentioned above,
that in each year we must add in the preparations for the Giving of the Torah, and particularly in the preparation of the precedence of "Naaseh" to "Nishma"
(on the eve of the festival of Shavuos),
and through this, also the matter of the Giving of the Torah and the receiving of the Torah on the festival of Shavuos is on a more elevated level,
to the point of being incomparable.
And so much so that in each year,
all these matters
(the Giving of the Torah and the receiving of the Torah,
and likewise the preparations for this)
are truly new.
And particularly in this year
the eve of the year 5750, which stands for—the acronym hints at "it will be a year of miracles"
(and also in this year,
the eve of 5750,
we already taste from the miracles of 5750),
the preparation must be with greater strength and vigor.
And through the addition from year to year in the preparations for the Giving of the Torah,
there is also addition in the matter of the Giving of the Torah,
to the point of an incomparable addition and in a manner of renewal.
For although the matter of the Giving of the Torah,
and in a manner of renewal,
is throughout all the days of the year
(as above in section 2),
nevertheless, the essence of the matter of the Giving of the Torah
(in a completely new manner)
is on the festival of Shavuos, the time of the giving of our Torah.
